races.name: Taste The World Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Marsh Benham
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner; Mr Simon Walker takes a horse with two recent wins over this course and trip in good ground, and the unchallenged lead is a significant tactical gift — though racing here from a hold-up profile tag means this prominent role is redistributed rather than natural, marginally tempering its style-fit score.
runners_data.comment: Marsh Benham arrives in fine fettle after winning last time out, and a second two starts back underlines his recent consistency; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 29 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough to go again off 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Kimeko Glory
runners_data.note: Charles Hills in a rich vein of form (T14: 4/22) and the four-year-old returns just eight days after its last run; history shows ten sim-going qualifications from fifteen, and racing forced closer than ideal may actually suit given its pace-in-to-finish profile — the trainer angle is the headline here.
runners_data.comment: Kimeko Glory has been knocking on the door, finishing third last time out and fourth two starts back, and she has run over today's distance and going before — our rating of 74 tops the field and makes her a leading threat; the risk is she remains yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Darvel
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old blinkered veteran with solid course-relevant form, placing three times over this course and distance in good ground; his true hold-up preference is nudged forward into midfield by the pack dynamics, and at STYLE_FIT 0.93 his chance is real only if he gets racing room rather than a clean rear run.
runners_data.comment: Darvel arrives on the back of a third two starts back and a second three starts back, showing consistent improvement that marks him as a genuine danger, and he returns fresh on 28 days' rest having run over today's distance and going; the concern is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Prince Rasam
runners_data.note: Only one sim-going qualification from ten is a serious flag on this good-to-firm Salisbury surface, and 86 days since last run adds freshness doubt; the Gary and Josh Moore yard is in form (T14: 4/22) but the going and layoff make him hard to trust, with his natural rear-of-field style also compressed forward.
runners_data.comment: Prince Rasam shaped well when second last time out and has run over today's trip, while a rating of 71 gives him a live chance from stall 8; the concern is a return from 86 days off having been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Prodigal Son
runners_data.note: Four-year-old trained by Heather Main, zero sim-going qualifications from twelve is a clear concern on this good-to-firm surface; Mr Henry Main (3lb claim) adds minor compensation, but the horse's true hold-up style is displaced into midfield and the going record is a genuine deterrent.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Prodigal Son has managed just one win in his last five starts, that victory coming five starts back, and a ninth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has experience over today's trip and going and returns just 29 days after his latest outing.

runners_data.name: Optimatum
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's charge steps back up to a mile having run poorly over six and seven furlongs recently; one sim-going hit from fourteen is worrying, and the natural hold-up tendency pushed into midfield creates an awkward scenario for a horse already out of recent form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though a second four starts back shows he can threaten at this level; the concern is back-to-back ninths bracketing that effort, and carrying 151 lb from stall 2 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Palazzo Persico
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old has two wins from fifteen in similar going and won at twelve furlongs last time, suggesting stamina rather than pure pace — at a mile on good-to-firm he may be outpaced late, though a clean wide run from a compressed field could flatter his effort; the trainer's strong recent strike rate (T14: 3/38 numerically modest) is noted.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Palazzo Persico faces a stiff task, and a fifth latest do little to inspire confidence; he has run over today's trip and going before, and his record does contain two wins in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Thiscouldbefun
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and won last time over this course and trip in good ground, which is the most directly relevant piece of form in the race; J S Moore's yard is in form (T14: 4/21) and Miss Dorricott's 5lb claim is useful, but the horse's naturally rear-running style is crowded into midfield, so replicating that Salisbury win requires a clear run it may not find.
runners_data.comment: Thiscouldbefun won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but her inconsistent recent record — unplaced two and four starts back — gives reason for caution, and 147 lb from stall one adds to the puzzle.

races.paceDynamic: Marsh Benham is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner amateur handicap over Salisbury's straight mile on good-to-firm ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead he will dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the off. The remainder of the field — Kimeko Glory, Darvel, Prince Rasam, Prodigal Son, Optimatum, Palazzo Persico and Thiscouldbefun — are all natural hold-up types who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would ideally prefer, crowding the midfield band and compressing the field. This creates a race that is likely to be run at an honest but unchallenged gallop, with Marsh Benham able to control the tempo and potentially steal a decisive advantage into the home straight. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Darvel, Prince Rasam, Prodigal Son, Optimatum, Palazzo Persico and Thiscouldbefun all jostling for midfield positions they do not naturally occupy — the shape most clearly favours those that can race prominently without over-exerting, as the compressed midfield will create traffic issues and a late finish is unlikely to be truly set up by the steady pace Marsh Benham will dictate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Benham Controls, Wins Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Marsh Benham dictates an unchallenged, measured gallop and the hold-up pack cannot generate the finishing burst to reel him in.
scenarios.body: Marsh Benham leads throughout at a controlled tempo on good-to-firm Salisbury, and with no pressure applied the amateur rider Mr Simon Walker can time his effort perfectly into the home straight, producing enough to hold any late challenge. This shape suits a horse that leads and quickens away; Marsh Benham's recent course-and-distance wins in similar going underpin this as the dominant scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften Marsh Benham and a hold-up horse finds a clear passage to deliver a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: One of the horses racing closer than ideal — Darvel or Thiscouldbefun — manages to track the pace from a handy position and times a strong run in the final furlong as Marsh Benham ties up. Darvel has placed form on this course and trip in similar going and represents the most credible late threat if his redistribution to midfield proves advantageous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed hold-up pack creates sustained interference and a horse wide of the trouble finds an unimpeded run to overhaul a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: With seven horses fighting for midfield and rear positions, horses on the outer — Palazzo Persico or Kimeko Glory — may benefit from a cleaner passage while those caught in traffic lose momentum at a critical stage. Palazzo Persico's course form on going-to-firm ground and recent winning form over a mile give this some credence as a chaos-beneficiary scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Hold-Up Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Marsh Benham sets a stronger gallop than anticipated and the race collapses into a sprint finish that a properly saved-for runner can win.
scenarios.body: A horse allowed to drop out and find room late — perhaps Prodigal Son or Prince Rasam if they fully settle — could produce a one-pace finish effort if the pace genuinely tests the field. This scenario is heavily discounted because the true hold-up types have been mapped forward and the conditions for a genuine swoop are unlikely to materialise with just one front-runner and a self-selecting tempo.

watchPoints.text: Marsh Benham's unchallenged lead could prove unassailable — watch whether Mr Simon Walker allows any daylight entering the home straight, as no horse appears positioned or motivated to press him early.

Darvel and Thiscouldbefun are the two most course-relevant hold-up horses forced into midfield; if either gets squeezed or checked in the final two furlongs, their chance evaporates — watch the draw and early positioning for signs of traffic.
Prince Rasam's going record (1 from 10 in sim conditions) is the most glaring stat in the race — if the ground rides genuinely quick it is a major red flag, worth monitoring at the off.

The amateur jockey element means pace judgement may be inconsistent — Mr Hezekiah March (7) on Prince Rasam and Miss Scarlett Dorricott (5) on Thiscouldbefun are less experienced claimers whose positional decisions in the first half-mile could reshape the whole traffic picture.

Palazzo Persico's stamina profile (two wins over ten and twelve furlongs) is worth tracking — if the pace is strong enough to stretch the field he may stay on when others flatten out, particularly if he gets a clean outside passage.

races.name: Robert Gilbert Birthday Celebration Irish EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Andy Hardwick & Clive Leonard Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Eternal Solace
runners_data.note: Returning after 88 days off, which is a meaningful fitness query for a hold-up horse who needs a strong end-to-end gallop to produce her best; Ollie Sangster's runner has placed at 6f on good ground before but the form string (32600) is trending the wrong way and a race with controlled fractions is unlikely to suit her from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and carrying 94 points of ability, Eternal Solace shaped with promise when second four starts back and third five starts back, yet recent outings have been disappointing and a 88-day absence after three winless efforts raises a fitness question she must answer.

runners_data.name: Zen Diva
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly arrives in the form of her life with two consecutive wins at 6f on good ground, and a prominent racing style means she is perfectly positioned to exploit a steady pace by tracking Kohana Nation and pouncing late; the drop into handicap company after two conditions wins is the key question, but the going is firmly in her favour.|
runners_data.comment: Zen Diva won two of her last five starts, including back-to-back victories before her latest run, and she arrives fit on 24 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going behind her, but that unplaced effort last time out is the one question mark to settle.

runners_data.name: Bintola
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's three-year-old won at 6f on good ground two starts ago and races prominently, making her well-suited to tracking the leader in this shape; she was beaten in a similar race last time (5th, 6f, Good) and must prove she can replicate that earlier form, but Lewis Edmunds keeps her competitive from a tracking position.|
runners_data.comment: Bintola showed she can win when landing the spoils three starts back, and she has experience of today's distance and going in her favour; a 39-day break is worth noting, but carrying 135 lb from stall 7 she is hard to ignore on her overall profile.

runners_data.name: Inca Heights
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is an important negative in a Salisbury 6f race that ends with a pronounced uphill climb; form figures on good ground include a win at 6f but more recently she has been beaten out of sight (6th, 11th, 12th, 13th), and the headgear notation (p) suggests connections have tried to address the issue without sustained success.|
runners_data.comment: Inca Heights shaped with promise when second five starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, while a trainer firing at 27% in the last fortnight keeps him firmly in the picture; the main worry is that he has been winless in recent starts and was only sixth last time out.

runners_data.name: Kohana Nation
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner who won over this exact course and distance on good ground 20 days ago, giving Jason Watson a clear tactical advantage to dictate every fraction; with no pace rival to force a duel, the risk of burning out is minimal, and Charles Hills has her fit and in form after a quickly-turned-around prep.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and well below several rivals on speed ratings, Kohana Nation is a tough sell despite winning last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him at least some grounding for the conditions.

runners_data.name: Havana Smile
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who has been pushed into the midfield map position because this field is backloaded with closers — in practice she is unlikely to get the true rear-group trip she needs to produce her best. Gary & Josh Moore's runner won over 5f on good ground but steps up to 6f, and the longer trip with a controlled pace and 7lb claim from Toby Moore is an unpredictable combination.|
runners_data.comment: Havana Smile won three starts back but has posted a sixth and fifth in his two most recent runs, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, 130 lb is a stiff burden to overcome as he tries to rediscover that winning thread.

runners_data.name: Coyy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's runner is a genuine hold-up type whose last ten runs are almost entirely at 5f — the step to 6f is an unexplored distance question. Coyy has been placed in the midfield map due to hold-up congestion rather than because she will race there by design; in a race with a slow pace set by an uncontested leader, a horse needing a strong gallop to close into is fighting the shape.|
runners_data.comment: Coyy won two starts back but has been unplaced on his most recent outing, and with a speed rating of 77 leaving him ranked sixth of seven on our figures, it is hard to make a case for him despite having run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Kohana Nation is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jason Watson should be able to dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Salisbury's straight 6f on good-to-firm ground. That uncontested lead creates a rail-to-rail scenario where Kohana Nation sets the fractions entirely on her own terms, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to manufacture the late momentum they need. Zen Diva and Bintola are the two genuine prominent types who will push forward to track the leader, giving the race a sensible shape with a covered gallop rather than a scorching tempo. This race shape strongly favours the lead-and-prominent profile — horses who can sit close to the pace and pounce in the final furlong — because the absence of pace pressure means the front runners' stamina reserves are preserved and a late finishing burst from deep is unlikely to be rewarded. Havana Smile and Coyy are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield because the field holds more hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear; neither is likely to secure the deep position they need, and both should be discounted in a shape that rewards position-keeping.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kohana Nation Leads & Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Kohana Nation dictates an uncontested, comfortable pace and the field fails to close.
scenarios.body: Watson sets fractions to suit over the straight 6f, arriving at the rising finish with petrol remaining; the controlled tempo denies closers the end-to-end gallop they need to generate a winning surge. Horses closest to the pace — Zen Diva and Bintola — are best placed to challenge but Kohana Nation, in winning form on similar ground, has fitness and confidence on her side.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Zen Diva or Bintola track the pace efficiently and use superior class to reel in Kohana Nation inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A well-judged stalking ride from either prominent mover puts them on the leader's quarters entering the final 2f; both carry form over exactly this trip and going combination, and Ralph Beckett's Zen Diva brings two recent wins in similar conditions. The slight rise to the Salisbury finish suits a horse arriving with momentum over a tiring front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a closer finds the track clear to deliver a strong late run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Kohana Nation to have gone too hard early — unlikely given the absence of any pace rival — and the midfield horses to find the sprint lane clear in the final furlong. Coyy and Havana Smile are the theoretical beneficiaries, but both are racing out of their natural hold-up role after redistribution, tempering confidence in this outcome significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners fail to handle the ground or encounter traffic issues, scrambling the result.
scenarios.body: Inca Heights or Eternal Solace, racing from off the pace with form figures that suggest inconsistency, could sneak into a place in a muddled finish if the principals disappoint. This is a low-probability tail risk given the clear pace structure, but the fitness of Eternal Solace returning after 88 days is a small unknown worth filing.

watchPoints.text: Kohana Nation — watch whether Jason Watson takes an immediate lead or allows an early push from Zen Diva or Bintola; if she is pressed even briefly in the opening furlong, the pace dynamic shifts and the lead scenario becomes less certain.

Zen Diva — watch the market: if Beckett's filly is supported into short odds, it reflects the form community rating two consecutive wins on identical going as the most serious threat to the front-runner.

Havana Smile and Coyy — both true hold-up horses running in a race that lacks the strong gallop they need; watch whether either jockey elects to ride more prominently than usual, which would signal the riders themselves are aware the natural style won't work here.

Inca Heights — watch for early signs of being pushed along before halfway; the finishing fade flag combined with this uphill track makes her a genuine candidate to be swamped in the final furlong even if she lies handily for much of the race.

races.name: Cara Glass Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Box Clever
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's three-year-old has placed twice on good ground and is the clear pace-setter here; his STYLE_FIT tag reflects he is mapping as a front-runner when his typical role is prominent, but in practice he is likely to go forward and dictate — five similar-going runs returned one win and four places, making him dangerous if the pace stays honest.
runners_data.comment: Box Clever shaped with clear promise when third last time out, and she has run over today's distance and going before — a filly who rates a leading danger here on a mark of 68, though the challenge is to finally convert that form into a win after going winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Court Of Stars
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's yard is in decent nick at 3/19 over 14 days and Stevie Donohoe takes a prominent-styled filly who has placed on good ground before; six of her last runs came on Stanmore going which differs from today's good-to-firm Salisbury, but she is consistent enough in form and should be suited to tracking Box Clever.
runners_data.comment: Rated 70 and ranked second of eight, Court Of Stars arrives fresh off a 15-day break having experienced today's trip and conditions, and her pair of seconds in recent starts highlight her place-finding ability — yet she remains winless in her last six, which is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Zipwire
runners_data.note: Taylor Fisher partners a hold-up filly who has run five times on good ground without troubling the judge; she returns just eight days after her last run and, while freshness is not a concern, her form string of 235654 on similar surfaces gives little confidence she can rattle home from the back in a potentially moderate gallop.
runners_data.comment: Zipwire has been winless in his last six starts, though a third five starts back and a second six starts back hint at ability, and he arrives on a quick eight-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going; the concern is a slide to fourth last time and a 133 lb burden from stall three.

runners_data.name: Footstepinthewoods
runners_data.note: Sean Levey is a strong booking and the key form asset here is a winning run at 8f on good ground — her natural hold-up style is a slight concern in a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo, but she is the most proven performer at this trip and surface combination in the field.
runners_data.comment: Footstepinthewoods arrives on the back of a win, and with experience of both today's trip and going conditions he looks a genuine threat at 131 lb from stall eight; the risk is that his last four starts before that victory showed inconsistency he will need to leave behind.

runners_data.name: Thisonesforyou
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up type by nature, pushed into the midfield slot on the map because the rear is over-crowded; Georgia Dobie rides and the filly has winning and placed form on both good and soft, though a true closer's race may not materialise from Box Clever's expected tempo.
runners_data.comment: Thisonesforyou shaped well when third two starts back and has experience over today's trip and conditions, while a trainer striking at 27% over the past fortnight adds appeal; drawn in stall four carrying 129 lb, he arrives fresh enough after 25 days off.

runners_data.name: Crimson Sunset
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's filly returns after 97 days off — the freshness flag is the primary concern — and, though she has placed form at this trip, her four recorded runs have all ended without a win and her true closer's instincts will be blunted by a controlled pace; the layoff and modest form make this a speculative proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and off the track for 97 days, Crimson Sunset has experience over today's trip and a straightforward draw in stall five, though a consistently mid-to-rear finishing pattern offers little immediate encouragement.

runners_data.name: Florizelle
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne's filly has only three runs to her name, all on soft or standard going, giving an UNKNOWN or at best modest reading for today's good-to-firm conditions; she is a natural hold-up horse bumped into midfield by overcrowding at the rear, and with the shortest form record in the field she faces the steepest learning curve.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Florizelle faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip before and draws stall one carrying 126 lb — small consolations for a filly who also returns after a 74-day absence.

runners_data.name: Violet Goldsmith
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's yard carries a high volume (4/38 in 14 days) but Violet Goldsmith brings the most relevant recent form — a win and a place both at 8f on good ground — and Charles Bishop takes over the ride; a genuine closer by nature, she is the hold-up type best equipped to make the finish if anything opens up late, despite being mapped forward of her preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our assessments, Violet Goldsmith faces a stiff ask against this field, yet she arrives on the back of a win and a second in her last two starts and has experience of today's trip and going, so she is not without hope at a fair weight.

races.paceDynamic: Box Clever is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push the pace from the front, Jason Watson can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout the mile at Salisbury. Court Of Stars is the one horse with prominent tendencies capable of pressing Box Clever, but the remainder of this field — Thisonesforyou, Crimson Sunset, Florizelle, and Violet Goldsmith — are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed with closers who cannot all get their natural position. The race shape points clearly to a steady-to-moderate pace under Box Clever's control, with a compressed midfield strung out behind, meaning the tempo will not be fast enough to naturally set up a strong late finish for pure closers. This scenario favours horses that can travel prominently in the slipstream of the front-runner and quicken from a close-up position — the prominent-to-midfield profile is the one to follow, with true hold-up types facing an uphill task if the pace is insufficient to stretch the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Box Clever Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Box Clever leads without serious pressure and sets a measured pace that suits a prominent-tracking winner.
scenarios.body: Box Clever bowls along at a fair but controlled gallop, dictating every yard through Salisbury's mile, and the winner comes from the group tracking him at close range; Court Of Stars is ideally placed to capitalise given her prominent style and recent form tightening at this grade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field and a close-tracking horse picks off Box Clever inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Box Clever sets enough tempo to be vulnerable late, and a horse sitting just off the leader within two lengths makes a decisive move; Footstepinthewoods, who has winning form at this trip on good ground, is capable of this style of finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Box Clever goes hard enough to collapse his own chance and the field fans wide turning for home, gifting closers a clear run.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop would need to materialise — unlikely given Box Clever's lone-ranger status — but if it does, Violet Goldsmith and Thisonesforyou, both with winning form on good ground at this trip, could motor past beaten rivals; the redistribution of so many hold-up types makes this a low-probability shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the race develops into a slow-burn sprint finish off a crawl.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race compresses the entire field and turns it into a dash over the final two furlongs, eliminating Box Clever's stamina edge and making high draw and sprint fitness the deciding factors; Zipwire's recent quick turnaround and Crimson Sunset's modest form at this level mean neither is ideally equipped even in this chaos.

watchPoints.text: Box Clever is the sole front-runner — watch whether Jason Watson is challenged early or left entirely alone, as an uncontested lead over 1m on good-to-firm ground gives him every chance to control the race tempo throughout.

Crimson Sunset returns after 97 days off the track; watch how sharply she moves in the paddock and early in the race, as ring-rustiness from a long absence could see her lose ground before the field has settled.

The four redistributed hold-up horses — Thisonesforyou, Crimson Sunset, Florizelle, and Violet Goldsmith — are all natural closers who cannot all secure their preferred position; watch for traffic issues and interference in the final two furlongs as they try to find daylight simultaneously.

Zipwire runs just eight days after her last start — watch whether J S Moore's team have freshened her for a quick turnaround or whether the tight schedule reflects a yard simply keeping a horse busy, as her hold-up style means she needs to arrive at the finish full of running.

races.name: Signs In Motion British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bintward
runners_data.note: The race pivots around this Roger Varian three-year-old — a winning front-runner returning on 22 days' rest who gets to lead unopposed here; his style fit is flagged at 0.90 meaning he's technically rated as slightly out of role, but in practice he is the lone pace-setter and stands to benefit most from the absence of any challenger.|

runners_data.name: Stopherandgo
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran for David Flood carrying a fade-in-finish flag and a dire recent form string of 0 and 7, with sim-going returns of 0 wins 0 places from six runs — his record offers no encouragement, and his hold-up style leaves him entirely dependent on a strong gallop that Bintward has no reason to provide.|

runners_data.name: That's All Folks
runners_data.note: Jeff Mullins's six-year-old is a hold-up type wearing hood who has finished no better than fifth in his last five starts across varying surfaces and distances, with a particularly uninspiring 0W0P record from five sim-going runs; a passive pace makes it very hard for him to produce a telling challenge.|

runners_data.name: Herstmonceux
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick's lightly-raced three-year-old has only one run to his name — a fifth over 8f on good — and his unknown tactical profile is the key unknown; if he travels prominently in behind Bintward, his unexposed profile gives him an each-way chance under Lewis Edmunds.|

runners_data.name: Golden Island
runners_data.note: Heather Main's three-year-old showed promise with a third on good ground over 10f last time, and his form angle is the most compelling among the closers; however, he is a true hold-up horse whose remapping to midfield overstates his likely pitch — he will sit deepest, and a slow pace under Bintward's control makes his task significantly harder than it might appear.|

races.paceDynamic: Bintward is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner novice over 1m2f at Salisbury on good-to-firm ground, and with no rivals willing or able to challenge for the lead, he will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. The three hold-up types — Stopherandgo, That's All Folks, and Golden Island — will settle in behind, while Herstmonceux's unknown style leaves him unpredictable in terms of positioning. With Bintward uncontested and able to control tempo to suit himself, this race is set up as a front-runner's benefit: a measured pace that denies closers the strong gallop they need to reel him in late. Golden Island is flagged as a true hold-up type remapped to midfield because the rear of the field is crowded with hold-up horses, but his natural instinct will be to sit deepest — meaning his shown midfield position overstates how well-placed he'll actually be. The race shape strongly favours Bintward and any horse capable of travelling prominently in second, as the absence of genuine pace pressure makes it very difficult for pure hold-up horses to generate the sustained momentum needed to close ground in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bintward Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bintward sets an uncontested, measured gallop and controls the race from the front throughout.
scenarios.body: Bintward dictates every fraction without pressure, building a winning break around the home turn that the hold-up horses simply cannot bridge on a good-to-firm surface; the lack of a genuine pace duel leaves closers with too little to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is slow enough that a horse tracking Bintward in second pounces turning in and overpowers him late.
scenarios.body: A dawdling pace compresses the field and one challenger times a run from second to wear down Bintward inside the final furlong; Herstmonceux, with lightly-raced upside, is best placed to exploit this position if he travels well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bintward sets a stronger-than-expected gallop that stretches the field and creates a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A genuinely honest pace would suit the closers by giving them something to race into, allowing the best-staying hold-up types to pick off the leader in the closing stages; Golden Island, with a third on similar going over 10f, is the most credible beneficiary, despite being a true hold-up type likely to be further back than his mapped position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If a slow pace creates a sprint finish that randomises the result and negates all running styles.
scenarios.body: With five runners and no pace duel, the race could collapse into a furlong-long dash that produces an untidy, bunched finish where finishing kick rather than stamina decides the outcome; this is the least likely scenario given the experienced hold-up brigade are unlikely to quicken sharply.

watchPoints.text: Bintward sets a crawl up front — if Ray Dawson conserves energy through the first mile, the hold-up horses behind will never get the gallop they need and Bintward's winning margin could be larger than expected.

Golden Island's true running position will be rearmost despite his midfield mapping — watch whether Jack Mitchell opts to push him forward early or accepts a disadvantageous position in a slowly-run race.

Herstmonceux is lightly raced and his tactical response to being tucked in behind a lone leader is completely unknown — a wide, eyecatching move around the home turn could signal he is better than his single run suggests.

Stopherandgo's fade-in-finish flag combined with his age (9) and poor sim-going record makes him a significant drifter in-running if the pace is modest — watch for him to drop back sharply entering the straight.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for the 7:27 slot, firmer than the declared Good — horses that have previous concerns on quick ground, particularly the hold-up types, should be monitored in the early betting for any market reaction.

races.name: Edwards Ford, Foray Motor Group Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Moab
runners_data.note: A veteran hold-up specialist over marathon trips with solid Good to Firm course form, though his last run was 115 days ago and he has never won beyond 16f — stamina here is fine but the layoff and his tendency to fill a place rather than win outright is the key angle.|
runners_data.comment: Moab shaped with real promise when third last time out and boasts a win three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the main concern is the 115-day absence.

runners_data.name: Digger One
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who will dictate the pace uncontested, but his recent form shows fading finishes and he has struggled on Good to Firm over comparable distances — the uncontested lead is an asset, yet his finishing fragility is a real risk in the closing stages.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Digger One faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's going before and returns on a quick turnaround of 16 days, but an eighth last time out does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Masterdream
runners_data.note: Excellent course and distance profile with multiple placed efforts on Good, and his true style is a genuine deep hold-up run best left to the final 2f — the trainer's poor 14-day strike rate (0/9) and nine-year age are noted, but on this going and trip his form stacks up well.|
runners_data.comment: Masterdream shaped well when second last time out and third three starts back, giving him solid recent claims, and he arrives fresh on 31 days' rest, carrying 137 lb over a trip and going he has experienced before, making him the one to beat despite being yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: Lightly-framed three-year-old taking a significant step up from 12f to 14f for the first time, yet three wins from 15 starts on Good ground and a jockey in Sean Levey who rides this trip assertively give her a clear angle — her natural hold-up style suits this shape if she can quicken cleanly.|
runners_data.comment: A Daughters Love arrives on the back of a second last time out and a win two starts back, boasting three wins in her last six starts and experience on today's going; the main risk is whether 134 lb proves too much to overcome.

runners_data.name: Basilette
runners_data.note: A horse whose best efforts have come over 16-18f on Good ground, wearing a hood and with two wins from 15 similar-going runs — naturally a deep hold-up type whose chance depends on whether the pace Digger One sets is strong enough to create a truly searching finish at the business end.|
runners_data.comment: Basilette shaped well enough for a third two starts back before landing the spoils three starts back, and she has experience of both today's trip and going; the main concern is that sixth on her latest outing leaves something to prove heading in.

runners_data.name: Panthere Noir
runners_data.note: A lightly-weighted three-year-old with a win and multiple places at shorter trips on Good, stepping up markedly in trip here — her natural deep hold-up style means she requires a strong gallop to bring her late finish into play, and the trip extension is an unknown that softens her claims.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, Panthere Noir is hard to fancy despite a relatively active recent spell, and his official mark of 52 leaves little room for optimism against stronger-rated rivals; that said, he was a winner two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Digger One is the lone confirmed front-runner and will stride into an uncontested lead from the off over this 1m6f trip at Salisbury, setting a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground without any rival genuinely threatening to push the pace from outside. With Moab, A Daughters Love, Masterdream, Basilette, and Panthere Noir all holding hold-up or deep hold-up profiles, the race will inevitably set up as a procession through the early and middle stages, with the real contest beginning only in the final quarter-mile when closers try to close the gap on Digger One's honest but limited lead. The field carries significantly more hold-up horses than can be realistically mapped to the rear — Masterdream, Panthere Noir, and Basilette are genuine deep closers redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning in practice the rear group will be congested and some will need to produce finishing kicks from an uncomfortable position. This race shape strongly favours a horse who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from midfield in the straight, as Digger One's uncontested lead means closers must produce a sustained, powerful finish rather than a short late burst — profile suits a strong stayer who handles Good to Firm and can quicken cleanly from second gear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Digger One Leads, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Digger One dictates an honest but uncontested pace and the hold-up horses must produce sustained finishes from the final 3f.
scenarios.body: Digger One sets a measured gallop throughout and reaches the turn for home with a clear advantage, forcing every rival to produce their effort simultaneously from the back straight; on Good to Firm ground the horse with the most potent sustained finish — rather than a sharp burst — lands the decisive blow.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Swamps Field
scenarios.trigger: If Digger One's front-running has sapped him by the final 2f and the best hold-up horse produces a sweeping run to nail him close home.
scenarios.body: Digger One, carrying the burden of a solo lead, begins to fade inside the final 2f, opening a gap for the strongest traveller from the chasing pack to cut him down; in this shape, a horse with strong Good to Firm form over 14f+ who has been running on powerfully in recent runs picks up the prize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Patient Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Digger One, whose form notes a tendency to fade in the finish, sets too strong an early tempo and the race degenerates into a test of stamina and finishing resolution.
scenarios.body: The field strings out as Digger One uncharacteristically quickens the early gallop, causing the race to become a stamina grind, and any horse who has been conserving energy through the middle of the race and handles this trip well finds himself ideally positioned.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse manages to sit closer than expected to Digger One and effectively claims a prominent position to challenge turning for home.
scenarios.body: With only one genuine front-runner, any runner who breaks well and elects to travel prominently rather than drop back finds themselves in a racing position that nullifies the hold-up pack's late finish; the winner in this shape is a horse whose best form has come when in touch with the pace on Good to Firm ground.

watchPoints.text: Digger One's fade tendency is the key pace watch — if he begins to visibly shorten stride entering the final 2f, the race opens up instantly for every hold-up horse in the field.

A Daughters Love is stepping up 4f in trip for the first time; watch her action in the back straight — if she's struggling to travel at the 1m mark the stamina question has answered itself before the finish.

Masterdream, Panthere Noir, and Basilette will all be looking for a clear run from a congested rear group — a bunched finish turning for home could see one or more of these genuine closers checked or short of room at a critical moment.

Moab's 115-day absence is the longest in the field; watch his early movement and how sharply Jason Watson asks him to travel — if he's sluggish from the gates he may lack the race fitness to sustain a challenge over 1m6f on quick ground.
